newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines trim some late-spring fares.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines trim some late-spring fares.

text.p: Trying to stimulate demand ahead of the peak summer travel season, several U.S. airlines trimmed some late-spring fares.

Trans World Airlines Inc said it will cut some fares on U.S. routes and on flights between the United States and Toronto by at least 50 percent. TWA also said fares to Milan, Madrid and Rome will be cut up to 35 percent.
TWA said the special fares are non-refundable. Domestic and Toronto fares are valid for travel between May 8 and June 15, while the other fares are valid between May 8 and June 30, the company said.
Airlines such as US Airways Group Inc and Delta Air Lines Inc quickly matched those fares cuts in competing markets.

Industry analysts said airline typically launch fare sales to generate demand during seasonal lulls. The special fares may help airlines get an early start to the peak summer travel season, analysts said.
